# Simulation stability and actuators

How large a physics timestep can you use when differential IK drives **position
actuators** and you call `step()` every tick? That depends on the **integrator**
(MuJoCo) and on whether the engine’s PD tracking matches what you expect (Motrix
on Menagerie Piper today does not).

The case study ([IK tracking](case-study-ik-tracking.qmd#case-study-ik-tracking))
defaults to **kinematic** integration — write `qpos`, call `forward`, never
`step`. That isolates Jacobian IK from actuator dynamics. Production stacks almost
always use the **dynamic** path: each tick compute a joint target, write `ctrl`,
integrate. This page measures that path.

## Control stack

Menagerie Piper uses `<position … kp="…" kv="…"/>` actuators: `ctrl` is a **target
joint angle**, and an internal PD produces torques during `step` ([State
I/O](state-sensors-and-actuators.qmd#state-sensors-and-actuators)).

Lockstep differential IK on top looks like:

```text
read EE pose  →  J, dx  →  q_des  →  ctrl[:] = q_des  →  step(dt)
```

Two loops are stacked:

1. **Outer (IK):** small workspace correction each tick (`α · dls(J, dx)`).
2. **Inner (actuator):** PD pulls `qpos` toward `ctrl` with stiffness `kp`.

If `dt` is too large for the inner loop — especially with **explicit** integrators
(`euler`, `rk4`) — joint velocities explode, the arm overshoots, and IK never
converges. **Implicit** integrators treat the stiff PD more stably and tolerate
much larger `dt` on MuJoCo.

### Instability in motion

Dynamic IK with **Euler** integration and **20 ms** timesteps (one IK tick per
`mj_step`) blows up within a few control cycles: the arm flails, position error
 grows to hundreds of millimetres, and joint velocities spike (MuJoCo warns about
 unstable accelerations).

  <source src="imgs/ik-tracking/piper_ik_instability.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

Regenerate:

```bash
uv sync --extra mujoco
uv run python scripts/render_ik_instability_video.py
```

The red sphere is the fixed reach target; the overlay tracks position error and
peak joint speed. Compare with the stable kinematic videos in [Case study: IK
tracking](case-study-ik-tracking.qmd#case-study-ik-tracking).

## Substeps vs decimation

The instability clip uses **lockstep**: IK runs once per physics step at the same
20 ms rate. Production stacks almost never do that — **physics is faster than
control**.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Δt_sim` | One `step()` — physics timestep (`model.opt.timestep`) |
| `Δt_ctrl` | Time between IK / policy updates |
| `n_sub` | **Substeps** per control tick: `n_sub = Δt_ctrl / Δt_sim` |
| **Decimation** | Same ratio, RL/sim jargon: sim steps per env (control) step |

**Substeps** names the inner loop: integrate the plant `n_sub` times with **held**
`ctrl` between outer IK updates.

**Decimation** names the outer loop: the controller is **decimated** relative to
physics — e.g. “decimation = 10” at `Δt_sim = 2 ms` ⇒ `Δt_ctrl = 20 ms` (50 Hz IK,
500 Hz physics). Isaac Lab’s `decimation` on `sim.step()` is this count ([Simulation
loop](the-simulation-loop.qmd#the-simulation-loop)).

Lockstep (what failed above):

```text
ctrl = ik(obs)
step(Δt_ctrl)          # IK rate = physics rate
```

Substepped / decimated (typical fix):

```text
ctrl = ik(obs)         # once per Δt_ctrl
repeat n_sub times:
    step(Δt_sim)       # hold ctrl — inner PD + integrator
```

Menagerie Piper defaults to `Δt_sim = 2 ms`. Running IK at 50 Hz (`Δt_ctrl = 20 ms`)
means **`n_sub = 10`** (decimation 10): keep Euler if you must, but do **not** set
`timestep = 20 ms` unless you switch to an implicit integrator.

Runnable comparison (same seed-0 reach target):

```bash
uv run python scripts/ik_substeps_demo.py
```

Lockstep Euler @ 20 ms fails; ten 2 ms substeps with the same 20 ms control period
passes reach tolerance with bounded velocities.

## Position vs motor actuators

Menagerie Piper uses **position** actuators: `ctrl[i]` is a **target joint angle**
and MuJoCo’s built-in PD (from `kp` / `kv` in MJCF) converts error into torque
inside every `step()`. See [Joint PD control](state-sensors-and-actuators.qmd#joint-pd-control) for the law and gain meaning.

**Motor** actuators are the other common MJCF type: `ctrl[i]` is a **joint
torque** (Nm). Nothing servos the joint for you — your controller must compute
`τ` and write it each tick.

| | Position (`<position>`) | Motor (`<motor>`) |
|---|---|---|
| `ctrl` | Target `q*` | Torque `τ` |
| Inner loop | Inside simulator (PD) | Your code (PD, impedance, RL, …) |
| Hold `ctrl` across substeps? | **Usually fine** — PD re-computes force from current `(q, q̇)` vs held `q*` every substep | **Risky** — held `τ` is wrong once `q` moves (zero-order hold on force) |
| Typical command rate | Controller / IK rate (50 Hz) | **Physics rate** (500 Hz) or faster |

### Same decimation, different hold semantics

At `Δt_sim = 2 ms`, `Δt_ctrl = 20 ms`, **`n_sub = 10`** (50 Hz IK, 500 Hz physics):

**Position + IK** — update `q_des` at 50 Hz, hold across substeps:

```text
q_des = ik(...)
repeat 10 times:
    ctrl = q_des          # held target; inner PD runs each substep
    step(2 ms)
```

**Motor + IK** — map `q_des` to torque with [joint PD](state-sensors-and-actuators.qmd#joint-pd-control). Holding `τ` computed once at 50 Hz fails
 on the Piper reach test (large error, |qvel| spikes). Recompute PD every substep:

```text
q_des = ik(...)           # still at 50 Hz
repeat 10 times:
    tau = Kp*(q_des - q) - Kd*qdot   # fresh torque every 2 ms
    ctrl = tau
    step(2 ms)
```

Runnable comparison (seed 0, implicitfast, same IK gains as Menagerie `kp`/`kv`):

```bash
uv run python scripts/actuator_control_demo.py
```

Example output:

```text
position control  ok    err=   5.0 mm  peak |qvel|=   0.4  — ctrl = q_des @ 50 Hz, held 10 substeps
motor    control  FAIL  err=  35.4 mm  peak |qvel|=  98.3  — ctrl = tau @ 50 Hz (PD once), held 10 substeps
motor    substep  ok    err=   5.0 mm  peak |qvel|=   0.4  — ctrl = tau recomputed every 2 ms substep
```

**Takeaway:** decimation/substeps solve “physics faster than IK.” For **position**
 actuators, holding **targets** at controller rate is standard. For **motor**
 actuators, holding **torques** at controller rate is not — run the force loop at
 substep rate (or use position actuators / implicit servos).

## Benchmark

`scripts/benchmark_ik_sim_dt.py` runs the same **reach** and **circle** tests as
`ik_tracking_demo.py`, but integrates with position actuators instead of writing
`qpos` directly:

```bash
bash scripts/fetch_menagerie_assets.sh
uv sync --extra sim
uv run python scripts/benchmark_ik_sim_dt.py          # full dt sweep
uv run python scripts/benchmark_ik_sim_dt.py --quick  # smoke (5 dt values)
```

Setup:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Robot | Menagerie Piper (`scene.xml`), seed 0 |
| Control | DLS IK, gain 0.35, damping 1e-2 |
| Per tick | `ctrl = q_des`, one `step(dt)` |
| Horizon | Scaled so wall-clock span ≈ kinematic demo (20 ms nominal tick) |
| Pass (reach) | final position error \< 5 mm, \|qvel\| \< 20 rad/s |
| Pass (circle) | final tracking error \< 26 mm (75% of 35 mm radius), stable |

MuJoCo sweeps all four integrators (`euler`, `rk4`, `implicit`, `implicitfast`).
Motrix exposes only `model.options.timestep` — MJCF `<option integrator=…>` is
ignored (same warning as [Two simulators](two-simulators.qmd#two-simulators)).

### Maximum stable `dt` (MuJoCo, seed 0)

| Integrator | Max `dt` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `euler` | **10 ms** | Explicit; blows up by 15 ms (large \|qvel\|) |
| `rk4` | **15 ms** | Slightly better than Euler, still explicit |
| `implicit` | **100 ms** | Fails at 125 ms (reach diverges) |
| `implicitfast` | **100 ms** | Menagerie default; same ceiling as `implicit` here |

Menagerie ships `timestep="0.002"` and `integrator="implicitfast"` — conservative
and appropriate for generic dynamics. For **position-actuator IK loops** on this
arm, MuJoCo tolerates up to **100 ms** with implicit integrators while explicit
ones cap out near **10–15 ms**.

### Motrix (dynamic path)

On the same Piper scene, **no tested `dt` passed both reach and circle** with
position actuators + `step`. Numerically the sim stays bounded (no NaNs), but the
EE error stays at centimetre scale (≈ 200 mm) even at 2 ms — far from the 5 mm
reach tolerance.

A minimal sanity check shows why: holding five joints fixed and commanding
`ctrl = 0.6` on `joint1` for 500 steps at 2 ms, MuJoCo reaches ≈ 0.60 rad on
joint1 while Motrix drifts joint2/joint5 to large angles and joint1 stalls near
0.47 rad. That is an **engine / model parity** issue on Menagerie Piper, not a
tuning knob in this repo. Until Motrix position-actuator tracking matches MuJoCo,
use **kinematic IK** (`ik_tracking_demo.py`) on Motrix and treat dynamic
`ctrl` + `step` IK as MuJoCo-only for this asset.

## Practical guidance

| Goal | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Learn / debug IK Jacobian | Kinematic loop in `ik_tracking_demo.py` (both backends) |
| Dynamic IK + actuators on Piper | MuJoCo, `implicit` or `implicitfast`, `dt` ≤ 100 ms |
| Larger `dt` with explicit integrator | Avoid for position-actuator IK; cap near 10–15 ms |
| Motrix + Piper Menagerie | Kinematic integration; verify dynamic control separately |
| Policy at 50 Hz, physics faster | Use substeps / decimation (below); hold `ctrl` between IK ticks |

When you move from kinematic `qpos` writes to dynamic `ctrl`, re-tune IK gain and
re-check stability at your chosen `dt` — the inner PD adds lag and effective
stiffness the Jacobian loop never sees in FK-only mode.
